root_cause_label: Spec-compliant services but wrong control interface (TCP monitor instead of required UNIX monitor socket) plus missing VGA parameter
one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent successfully ran QEMU with VNC, nginx, and websockify but violated the benchmark contract throughout by using a TCP monitor (127.0.0.1:4444) instead of the required UNIX socket at /tmp/qemu-monitor.sock and by omitting the explicit -vga cirrus parameter, never recognizing these gaps.
t_err_evidence: Step 11: first successful QEMU launch uses '-display vnc=:1 -snapshot -daemonize' with no -vga flag and no monitor socket; the agent treats the VM as correctly configured despite both required parameters being absent.
t_commit_evidence: Step 29: after killing the old instance, the agent relaunches QEMU with '-monitor tcp:127.0.0.1:4444,server,nowait' (still no -vga cirrus, no UNIX socket); this configuration is never corrected in subsequent steps and persists until the end of the trajectory.
trigger_explanation: The task spec requires programmatic keyboard input 'for automated testing', implying the test harness needs a specific interface (UNIX monitor socket). The agent never considers what interface format the benchmark tests will use, instead defaulting to the convenient TCP monitor and never adding -vga cirrus. Both omissions persist from the first successful launch through completion.
forewarning_evidence: Step 10: KVM error forces a relaunch; this presented an opportunity to add -vga cirrus and a proper monitor socket, but the agent only removed -enable-kvm in step 11, missing the other required parameters.
